summary.text: Harriet Hageman is Wyoming's at-large U.S. Representative and the Republican nominee for the state's open U.S. Senate seat in 2026. A Wyoming attorney for more than three decades, she was elected to the House in 2022 after defeating incumbent Liz Cheney in the Republican primary. She chairs a House Natural Resources subcommittee and serves on the Judiciary Committee.

paragraphs.text: Hageman was born in Douglas, Wyoming, in 1962. According to her House office, she grew up on a ranch and attended Casper College on a livestock judging scholarship.
She earned a bachelor's degree in business administration in 1986 and a law degree in 1989, both from the University of Wyoming.

Hageman worked as a law clerk for federal appeals judge James E. Barrett, as a lawyer and as an adjunct professor. Her House biography says she was a litigator for 34 years and is admitted to practice before the U.S. Supreme Court.
She co-founded the Wyoming Conservation Alliance and, according to Ballotpedia, was one of the chief litigators opposing the 2001 Roadless Rule.
Hageman ran for Governor of Wyoming in the 2018 Republican primary and finished third with 21.5%, behind Mark Gordon and Foster Friess.
In 2022 she won the Republican primary for Wyoming's at-large House seat, defeating incumbent Liz Cheney, then won the general election; she was re-elected in 2024.

In the 119th Congress she chairs the Natural Resources Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife, and Fisheries, also serves on its Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee and the Judiciary Committee, and is Co-Chair of the Congressional Coal Caucus.
On August 18, 2026, she won the Republican primary for U.S. Senate, defeating Samuel Mead and three others, for the seat Sen. Cynthia Lummis is leaving.
